description: A sprawling, hollow-stemmed perennial of cold running water, floating and rooting in mats in the shallows, with dark green leaves of three to nine round leaflets and small white four-petalled flowers in short clusters. Brought from Europe as a salad green, it now fills the shallow edges of the spring-fed creeks and seeps, green all winter.

season_notes.winter: Dark green mats in the cold shallow water, one of the few fresh greens of the season.
season_notes.spring: Mats thicken and stems rise; small white flowers from April.
season_notes.summer: Flowering into August; where the creek dries the mats wither on the stones.
season_notes.fall: Fresh growth again as the water cools.

riparian.water: Lives in shallow, cool, clear, slowly running water, rooted in the mud and gravel of the bed: spring-fed creeks, seeps and ditches, and the shallows of ponds fed by springs.

notes: Watercress is a European perennial, naturalized throughout California in springs, seeps, slow clear streams and ditches; in the foothills it fills the shallow, cool, spring-fed reaches of small creeks. Habit sprawling: hollow stems trail and float, rooting at the nodes, forming mats 10-50 cm high (the module draws the sprawl on the wet bed and the shallows). Leaves alternate, odd-pinnate with three to nine (to thirteen) roundish leaflets, the end one largest, dark glossy green: leaf shape pinnate, 8 cm. Flowers small (4-5 mm), white, four petals, in short racemes elongating in fruit, April-August (on through the year in mild places): flower shape tiny, white. It grows through the winter in the water, so height_by_month stays 0.7 and up all year; where the creek dries in late summer it withers (dead_rgb). Introduced (native false); the native yellow cresses (Rorippa) of the same places are not drawn. Deer and quail eat the greens. Zones: in the channel of small perennial creeks (channel 1.0), the wet margin, a spring-fed pond's shallows; orders [1, 4], permanence perennial. shades_water 0.
